tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description starts with 'Use this skill when...' (imperative phrasing) and lists explicit trigger contexts: HTTP 403/405/202 responses, 4xx spikes, outages where WAF must be ruled out, finding which rule blocked requests, false positives, and threat hunting in WAF logs. It focuses on user-facing symptoms and intents (users denied access, investigation requests) rather than purely internal mechanics, though the second half does briefly mention implementation (Web ACL discovery, CloudWatch/Athena). It remains reasonably concise given the breadth of trigger scenarios it needs to cover.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when an investigation is about users, partners, scripts, or mobile apps that are denied access to or can't reach an application behind AWS WAF (HTTP 403, 405, 202 challenge responses, a 4xx spike, or an outage...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into domain-specific procedures (mode selection, discovery steps D-1 to D-7, query IDs, output contract) without explaining general concepts the agent already knows. It is dense but every sentence conveys project-specific facts.
tests.evidence: D-1 Resource to Web ACL: CloudFront GetDistributionConfig WebACLId; regional resources wafv2:GetWebACLForResource.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (query bodies, label tables, remediation pattern details, output contract specifics) are consistently delegated to references/ files rather than embedded in the body, even inside conditional branches like Mode A/B steps.
tests.evidence: Read [access-denied-triage.md](references/access-denied-triage.md) when Mode A runs; it holds the detail of each step.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown link syntax in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by a clear condition specifying when to load it (e.g., 'at the start of every run', 'when Mode A runs', 'when you bind placeholders').
tests.evidence: Read [access-denied-triage.md](references/access-denied-triage.md) when Mode A runs; it holds the detail of each step.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All references use relative paths from the skill root in the correct references/filename.md format.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, high-consequence operations (read-only guarantee, exact query IDs, mitigation guardrails, defang rule) are prescriptive with exact steps, while judgment-heavy areas (verdict classification, confidence levels, finding narration) allow for reasoned judgment with explained criteria.
tests.evidence: Never run DDL. Never change a Web ACL, rule, IP set, Shield setting, log configuration or any other resource.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: When multiple query backends or approaches exist (Athena vs Logs Insights), the skill designates clear defaults based on log destination, and fallback paths are described as degraded alternatives rather than equal options.
tests.evidence: Log group: Logs Insights. S3 or Firehose to S3: Athena. None, or a non-S3 destination without a full S3 backup: degraded path.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable investigative approach (mode selection, discovery, query binding, verdict reasoning) that applies across different incidents and hunts, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Classify, and record the choice under "Assumptions".

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill is rich with environment-specific gotchas interwoven throughout (e.g., region rules, wording pitfalls, token posture nuances) even without a dedicated 'Gotchas' heading.
tests.evidence: Wording alone never clears WAF (a 202 with an empty body is often reported as "timeout").
